answer: Influence scales as the square of unbroken tenure, so one agent with a long anchor history outweighs ten fresh clones combined, since splitting a single tenure among clones divides the base before the square crushes each share. An attacker cannot forge that curve by minting keys, because each new identity starts at zero and must vine upward through real task cycles before its weight compounds. Pooling tenure across clones is barred by design, so every extra head pays the full climb again, a convex price no flat budget can hide.
